formats.key: SafeTx(address to,uint256 value,bytes data,uint8 operation,uint256 safeTxGas,uint256 baseGas,uint256 gasPrice,address gasToken,address refundReceiver,uint256 nonce)
effects: With operation Call, the Safe sends `value` in native currency to `to` and runs `data` as a call from the Safe. This can be any token transfer, approval, or owner, module or guard change.
With operation DelegateCall, the Safe runs the code at `to` inside its own account, with full control of its balances and storage. No `value` is sent.

If gasPrice > 0, the Safe pays (gasUsed + baseGas) * gasPrice in gasToken to refundReceiver. A zero gasToken means ETH, with the price capped at tx.gasprice. A zero refundReceiver means tx.origin. The payment is made even when the inner call fails.
safeTxGas caps the gas of the inner call when gasPrice > 0, so it bounds the refund. When it is not zero, the inner call can fail without a revert while the nonce and the refund are still spent.
The Safe nonce goes up by one.
formats.shown: The intent 'Safe' plus raw fields: To, Value in ETH, Operation type, Transaction as nested calldata (raw hex in both tests), and Gas amount, Gas price, Gas token and Gas receiver as raw values. safeTxGas and nonce are hidden.

findings.title: SafeTx decodes data as a call to `to` with the Safe as sender, even for a DelegateCall
findings.evidence: descriptor.json, field `data`: "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "to", "amountPath": "value", "spenderPath": "@.to"}, with no condition on `operation`. Executor.sol execute(): `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, ...) }`. Test case 1 has operation 1 (Delegate Call) to MultiSend 0x3886...B526.
findings.fix: Decode `data` as a call to `to` only when operation is 0. For operation 1, show a fixed warning, or use a separate format or a mustMatch/ifNotIn guard. Only known delegate-call targets such as MultiSend should be decoded, with their own descriptor.

findings.title: SafeTx intent 'Safe' does not say that the Safe executes a transaction or a delegate call
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Safe". Both cases render the intent 'Safe', for an ETH transfer and for a MultiSend delegate call alike.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Execute Safe transaction". Add an interpolatedIntent such as "{operation} to {to} with {value}".

findings.title: SafeTx case 1 shows the MultiSend batch, a 1000 USDC transfer, only as raw hex
findings.evidence: cases/1.json, screen field 'Transaction' value '0x8d80ff0a...a9059cbb...e57f3834...3b9aca00...'. The batch holds USDC transfer(0xe57f..., 1000000000), which is 1000 USDC out of the Safe. Nothing readable states it.
findings.fix: Add a nested descriptor for MultiSend multiSend(bytes) as a delegate-call target, or a test that resolves the inner transfer. The test now proves only the raw fallback.

findings.title: SafeTx hides safeTxGas, which bounds the gas refund and lets the inner call fail silently
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: {"label": "Safe Tx Gas", "path": "safeTxGas", "visible": "never"}. Safe.sol execTransaction: `execute(..., gasPrice == 0 ? (gasleft() - 2500) : safeTxGas)`; `require(success || safeTxGas != 0 || gasPrice != 0, "GS013")`; `payment = handlePayment(gasUsed, baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken, refundReceiver)`.
findings.fix: Make safeTxGas visible as a raw field labelled "Max gas for the call".

findings.title: SafeTx shows gasPrice and gasToken raw; a zero gasToken means ETH
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: gasPrice "format": "raw"; gasToken "format": "raw". Safe.sol handlePayment: `if (gasToken == address(0)) { payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice < tx.gasprice ? gasPrice : tx.gasprice); ... } else { ... transferToken(gasToken, receiver, payment) }`. Case 0 shows Gas token '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'.
findings.fix: Show gasPrice as tokenAmount with "tokenPath": "gasToken" and "nativeCurrencyAddress": ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"]. Show gasToken as addressName or token.

findings.title: SafeTx shows a zero refundReceiver literally; the code pays tx.origin instead
findings.evidence: Safe.sol handlePayment: `address payable receiver = refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver;`. descriptor.json: refundReceiver "format": "raw", label 'Gas receiver'. Cases 0 and 1 show '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'.
findings.fix: Use addressName with "senderAddress": ["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"], or a label that says that zero means the executor.

findings.title: SafeTx labels baseGas 'Gas amount', but it is only fixed gas added to the gas the call uses
SafeTx shows Value as ETH sent even when operation is DelegateCall, which sends no value
findings.evidence: Executor.sol execute(): delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0) has no value argument. descriptor.json: value "format": "amount", visible always, no condition on operation.
findings.fix: Hide or relabel Value when operation is 1, or add a test for a delegate call with a non-zero value.

findings.title: SafeTx binds to the Safe 1.4.1 singleton, but real Safe proxies sign with their own address
findings.evidence: Safe.sol domainSeparator(): `keccak256(abi.encode(DOMAIN_SEPARATOR_TYPEHASH, getChainId(), this))`. Under a proxy, `this` is the proxy. descriptor.json eip712.deployments lists only 0x41675C...461a, the singleton. Its constructor sets threshold = 1 with no owners, so it executes nothing.
findings.fix: ERC-7730 has no factory or singleton constraint for EIP-712. Track this as a spec limitation.

couldNotCheck: Test case 1 delegate-calls MultiSend at 0x38869bf66a61cF6bDB996A6aE40D5853Fd43B526. Its source is not in the directory, so what the batch does inside the Safe could not be checked from code.

findings.title: SafeTx decodes data as a call to `to` with the Safe as sender, even for a DelegateCall
findings.reason: Executor.execute runs a delegatecall when operation is 1, so `to`'s code runs in the Safe's own context. The descriptor still decodes `data` as a plain call to `to` for any operation, with no condition. The screen does show 'Operation type: Delegate Call', but the nested decode does not change to match it. The severity guide lists this exact pattern as a calibrated critical, and test case 1 uses operation 1 to MultiSend.
